hits.title: Robo Inc. Launches US Humanoid Robot Integrator; China Spy Law Still Follows Hardware
hits.snippet: RoboStore, North America's most active distributor of humanoid and quadruped robots, today publicly launched **Robo Inc.**, a US-based manufacturing and systems integration company designed to fill the compliance gap left by the Federal Communications Commission's [July 28 decision](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DOC-423682A1.pdf) to block new Chinese-made advanced robots from the American market. The company says it will open a 66,000-square-foot (roughly 6,130 square meters) facility on Long Island, New York, expected to be operational by January 2027 — a concrete deadline and a named address in a sector that has historically offered neither. The launch arrives at a moment when the American robotics market is genuinely stuck. Chinese manufacturers currently account for approximately 51 percent of global humanoid robot production, with companies like Unitree offering fully operational humanoids starting at $13,500 — a price that domestic American manufacturers cannot match. hits.snippet: RoboStore, a major distributor of Chinese-made robots, is pushing to manufacture its systems domestically following the [US ban on foreign-made advanced robots](https://ca.pcmag.com/topic/17114/the-fccs-next-target-foreign-made-humanoid-robots-and-power-inverters).
